hero.headline: TELL CONGRESS: SUPPORT THE KARLY RAIN WOOD ACT
hero.ask: Ask your members of Congress to support and help advance the Karly Rain Wood Act, S. 5245.
reasons: Karly Rain Wood was 20, building a future and a business of her own, when repeat violent offenders took her life — and her case is still unsolved.
This bill creates a national registry so law enforcement agencies actually talk to each other about repeat violent offenders, instead of losing track at the state line.
It gives communities real safety information about who's moving in next door — before another family gets the call Amber got.

sidebar._note: Powers the simplified two-panel sidebar (photo + The Ask + The Details), modeled on the ANCOR/VoterVoice reference layout. Keep this short — the whole point of that layout is that it's NOT a wall of text.
sidebar.askBody: Ask your members of Congress to support and help advance the Karly Rain Wood Act, S. 5245.
detailsBody: The Karly Rain Wood Act would create a national registry and notification program at the U.S. Department of Justice for repeat violent offenders — strengthening communication between law enforcement jurisdictions and giving communities real safety information.
It's named for Karly Rain Wood, a 20-year-old Nebraska woman shot and killed by repeat violent offenders in November 2022. Her case remains unsolved.
sidebar.ctaLine: Contact your members of Congress today and urge them to support the Karly Rain Wood Act.

messageStep.title: Personalize and send your message
messageStep.subjectLine: Please Support the Karly Rain Wood Act – S. 5245
messageStep.letterBody:
I'm writing as your constituent to ask you to support and help advance the Karly Rain Wood Act, S. 5245.

This bill creates the Karly Rain Wood Repeat Violent Felon Registration and Notification Program at the Department of Justice — a national system to register and track repeat violent offenders and notify the public, so law enforcement agencies actually communicate across state lines and communities have the safety information they deserve. It's named for Karly Rain Wood, a 20-year-old Nebraska woman killed by repeat violent offenders in November 2022 in a case that remains unsolved.

This bill matters to our community, and I'm asking you to co-sponsor it and push for a vote. Please let me know where you stand.

Thank you for your time and your service.
messageStep.personalizeBoxSubtitle: Optional but encouraged: tell them why this matters to you, your family, or your community.
messageStep.personalizeNote: Congressional offices count individual, personalized messages very differently from identical form letters — a sentence or two in your own words makes this count more.

why.title: Karly's story
body: Karly Rain Wood was born in Omaha, Nebraska, in April 2002. The people who knew her describe her as unapologetically herself — someone who made everyone around her feel seen, heard, and appreciated. She once told her mother, Amber, "I don't want to be famous, I want to be successful."
She worked multiple jobs while teaching herself nail art, hair, makeup, cooking, and baking, and was saving to open her own beauty business and buy a home of her own.
On November 13, 2022, at 20 years old, Karly was shot and killed by repeat violent offenders after attending her first-ever party. Her case remains unsolved.
Since then, her mother Amber has turned grief into advocacy — for other victims, and for the legislation that carries her daughter's name.
why.pullQuote: Inspire confidence. Love who you are. Believe in yourself.

billSummary.title: What the Karly Rain Wood Act actually does
points: Establishes the Karly Rain Wood Repeat Violent Felon Registration and Notification Program inside the U.S. Department of Justice.
Creates a national system to register and track repeat violent offenders, instead of leaving that information siloed state by state.
Strengthens communication between law enforcement jurisdictions and notifies the public, giving communities real safety information about repeat violent offenders.
billSummary.fullTextLabel: Read the full bill text on Congress.gov

billStatus.title: Bill status
billStatus.statusNote: S. 5245 (119th Congress) was introduced in the U.S. Senate on August 5, 2026, by Senator Pete Ricketts (NE), with Senator Deb Fischer (NE) as a Senate co-sponsor. It has been referred to the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, where it now awaits a hearing or committee vote before it can move to the full Senate.

items.question: What is the Karly Rain Wood Act?
Why does my message need to be personalized?
items.answer: Congressional staff read every message that comes in, but they weigh personal, original messages more heavily than identical form letters when gauging genuine constituent concern. A sentence or two in your own words goes a long way.

items.question: I don't live in a state with a sponsor — should I still take action?
items.answer: Yes. Every constituent message to every office, sponsor or not, helps build momentum and signals nationwide support.
